note: Editorial shopping picks. Opening days, hours and prices change; check before you go.

tokyo.note: Tokyo rewards district-hopping: each neighbourhood has its own shopping personality, from Harajuku street style to Ginza flagships.

spots.name: Takeshita Street
spots.summary: A narrow, loud lane of kawaii fashion, cheap accessories, sock shops and crêpe stands.
spots.tip: Go on a weekday morning; weekend afternoons are shoulder to shoulder.

spots.name: Shimokitazawa vintage shops
spots.summary: Tokyo’s secondhand-clothing capital, with dozens of thrift and vintage stores plus records and cafés.
spots.tip: Prices range from bargain bins to collector pieces; check tags carefully for condition notes.

spots.name: Ura-Harajuku (Cat Street & backstreets)
spots.summary: The backstreets behind Omotesando where Japanese streetwear grew up: sneaker shops, small label stores and curated vintage.
spots.tip: Walk Cat Street from Harajuku toward Shibuya and duck into the side lanes; many shops open around 11:00.

spots.name: Shibuya Parco & Shibuya 109
spots.summary: Parco mixes Japanese designer labels with gaming and anime floors; 109 is the landmark for young women’s fashion.
spots.tip: Parco’s Nintendo and Pokémon floors get queues on weekends; go early.

spots.name: Ginza flagships & Dover Street Market
spots.summary: Global flagships, Mitsukoshi and Matsuya department stores and Dover Street Market Ginza’s avant-garde designer floors.
spots.tip: Bring your passport for tax-free purchases above the store minimum.

spots.name: Omotesando Hills & avenue
spots.summary: A tree-lined avenue of architect-designed flagships and Japanese designer labels.
spots.tip: Combine with Ura-Harajuku; the luxury avenue and streetwear lanes are minutes apart.

kyoto.note: Kyoto shopping leans toward craft: tea, textiles, ceramics and knives, with a compact modern centre around Shijo.

spots.name: Nishiki Market
spots.summary: A covered food street with pickles, tea, sweets and a few knife and kitchen shops.
spots.tip: Eating while walking is discouraged; eat at the stall or a designated area.

spots.name: Teramachi & Shinkyogoku arcades
spots.summary: Covered arcades with souvenir shops, sneaker stores, secondhand clothes and casual fashion.
spots.tip: Teramachi’s northern stretch has calmer antique and stationery shops.

spots.name: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka slopes
spots.summary: Stone lanes toward Kiyomizu-dera lined with ceramic, sweets and craft shops in old townhouses.
spots.tip: Visit before 9:00 or after 17:00 to see the lanes without the crowds.

spots.name: Kyoto Handicraft Center
spots.summary: A multi-floor store of Japanese crafts, woodblock prints, ceramics and kimono-style goods.
spots.tip: Tax-free shopping is available with your passport.

spots.name: Takashimaya & Daimaru Kyoto
spots.summary: Full department stores with designer floors and excellent basement food halls for gift boxes.
spots.tip: The food basements are ideal for packaged sweets that travel well.

osaka.note: Osaka is bargain-friendly and street-smart: covered arcades, streetwear in Amerikamura and big department stores in Umeda.

spots.name: Amerikamura
spots.summary: Osaka’s youth-culture hub with secondhand clothes, sneaker shops and skate-style streetwear.
spots.tip: Triangle Park is the centre point; shops open late morning and stay busy into the evening.

spots.name: Den Den Town
spots.summary: Osaka’s answer to Akihabara: electronics, retro games, figures and anime goods.
spots.tip: Check region compatibility and voltage before buying electronics.

spots.name: Shinsaibashi-suji & Midosuji
spots.summary: A long covered arcade of mid-range fashion and drugstores next to Midosuji’s luxury boulevard.
spots.tip: Drugstores here are popular for Japanese skincare; compare prices between branches.

spots.name: Kuromon Market
spots.summary: A covered market for seafood, fruit and snacks, with packaged foods to take home.
spots.tip: Prices are higher than local supermarkets; it is about tasting more than stocking up.

spots.name: Hankyu Umeda department store
spots.summary: One of Japan’s biggest department stores, with luxury brands and a famous food hall.
spots.tip: Combine with Grand Front Osaka and LUCUA in the same station complex.

seoul.note: Seoul is a trend capital: K-beauty, independent fashion labels and huge night-time wholesale markets.

spots.name: Dongdaemun fashion towers
spots.summary: Wholesale and retail fashion malls, some open until the early hours, next to the Dongdaemun Design Plaza.
spots.tip: Retail-friendly buildings like Doota welcome tourists; some wholesale floors sell only in bulk.

spots.name: Hongdae streets
spots.summary: Student-area fashion with local labels, vintage, character goods and late-night street life.
spots.tip: Weekend afternoons bring busking and a free market near Hongik University.

spots.name: Seongsu-dong
spots.summary: Former warehouses turned concept stores, pop-ups and Korean designer labels.
spots.tip: Pop-up stores change weekly; check social media for what is on.

spots.name: Garosu-gil
spots.summary: A tree-lined street of Korean and international fashion brands and cafés.
spots.tip: Side alleys hold the more independent boutiques.

spots.name: Cheongdam-dong & Galleria
spots.summary: Seoul’s luxury strip with global flagships and the Galleria department store.
spots.tip: Ask about tax refunds at purchase; many stores offer instant refunds.

taipei.note: Taipei mixes night-market bargains with design shops and polished malls around Taipei 101.

spots.name: Ximending
spots.summary: Taipei’s youth district with streetwear, sneakers, anime goods and street food.
spots.tip: Evenings and weekends are lively; the pedestrian zone is car-free.

spots.name: Raohe Street Night Market
spots.summary: A classic night market with cheap clothes, trinkets and snacks under lanterns.
spots.tip: Start at Ciyou Temple and walk the single main lane.

spots.name: Zhongshan & Chifeng Street
spots.summary: Small design studios, vintage shops and cafés along quiet lanes near the MRT line park.
spots.tip: Many shops open around noon and close one weekday; afternoons are the safe bet.

spots.name: Huashan 1914 Creative Park
spots.summary: A former winery with Taiwanese design shops, exhibitions and markets.
spots.tip: Weekend markets add independent makers; check the event calendar.

spots.name: Xinyi District malls
spots.summary: Taipei 101 Mall, Breeze Nan Shan and Shin Kong Mitsukoshi for luxury and global brands.
spots.tip: Skybridges connect most of the malls, which helps in rain.

hong-kong.note: Hong Kong is built for shopping: street markets in Kowloon, malls everywhere, and flagships in Central and Tsim Sha Tsui.

spots.name: Ladies’ Market
spots.summary: A long street market for clothes, accessories and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Bargain politely; branded items here are usually not genuine.

spots.name: Mong Kok sneaker street (Fa Yuen Street)
spots.summary: A strip of sneaker shops with a huge range of sizes and releases.
spots.tip: Compare stores: prices on the same shoe vary block by block.

spots.name: PMQ
spots.summary: Former police married quarters now filled with Hong Kong designer studios.
spots.tip: Studios open from late morning; some close one weekday.

spots.name: Harbour City
spots.summary: A huge waterfront mall with hundreds of brands from high street to luxury.
spots.tip: Ocean Terminal deck has free harbour views.

spots.name: Landmark & IFC
spots.summary: Hong Kong’s luxury core, with flagships and Lane Crawford.
spots.tip: Hong Kong has no sales tax, but compare prices with home first.

singapore.note: Singapore shopping is polished and air-conditioned, with character in Haji Lane, Little India and Chinatown.

spots.name: Bugis Street & Haji Lane
spots.summary: Budget fashion stalls at Bugis Street, then indie boutiques and street art on Haji Lane.
spots.tip: Haji Lane shops open around noon and are liveliest in the evening.

spots.name: Mustafa Centre
spots.summary: A sprawling, famous department store selling almost everything, at value prices.
spots.tip: It is open very long hours; late night is calmer.

spots.name: Chinatown Complex & Pagoda Street
spots.summary: Souvenir lanes and market stalls for gifts, tea and trinkets.
spots.tip: The hawker centre upstairs in Chinatown Complex is good for lunch.

spots.name: Orchard Road
spots.summary: A long boulevard of malls covering everything from high street to department stores.
spots.tip: ION Orchard and Takashimaya are good anchors; tourist GST refunds apply above the minimum spend.

spots.name: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
spots.summary: Luxury flagships under one roof by the bay.
spots.tip: Combine with the evening light show on the waterfront.

bangkok.note: Bangkok is a bargain hunter’s city with huge markets, but also has some of Asia’s grandest malls.

spots.name: Pratunam Market
spots.summary: A wholesale-style clothing market with very cheap fashion.
spots.tip: Mornings are best; many stalls sell in bulk but most accept single purchases.

spots.name: Platinum Fashion Mall
spots.summary: Air-conditioned floors of small fashion stalls at near-wholesale prices.
spots.tip: Buying three items often gets a lower per-piece price.

spots.name: Siam Square & Siam Center
spots.summary: Thai designer labels, youth fashion and streetwear around the Siam BTS hub.
spots.tip: Siam Center focuses on Thai designers; Siam Square’s lanes have smaller shops.

spots.name: ICONSIAM
spots.summary: A riverside megamall with luxury brands and SookSiam, an indoor floating-market food and craft hall.
spots.tip: Take the free shuttle boat from Sathorn pier.

spots.name: Siam Paragon & Central Embassy
spots.summary: Bangkok’s luxury malls with international flagships and gourmet food halls.
spots.tip: Ask for the VAT refund form on purchases above the minimum.

chiang-mai.note: Chiang Mai is a craft city: walking-street markets, handmade textiles and design studios in Nimman.

spots.name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar
spots.summary: A nightly market of souvenirs, clothes and crafts along Chang Khlan Road.
spots.tip: Bargaining is expected, but smile and keep it friendly.

spots.name: Warorot Market
spots.summary: A local market for snacks, fabrics and everyday goods.
spots.tip: Upper floors have hill-tribe textiles and cheaper fabric.

spots.name: Nimmanhaemin Road
spots.summary: Trendy lanes with Thai labels, design shops and cafés.
spots.tip: One Nimman holds a weekend craft market.

spots.name: Baan Kang Wat
spots.summary: An artists’ village with studios, ceramics and handmade goods.
spots.tip: Visit Sunday morning for its small market.

spots.name: Bo Sang & San Kamphaeng craft road
spots.summary: Umbrella makers, silk weavers and lacquer workshops with higher-end handmade pieces.
spots.tip: Ask to see work in progress; quality varies, so compare a few workshops.

hanoi.note: Hanoi’s Old Quarter streets are still organised by trade, with silk, lacquer and design shops around Hoan Kiem Lake.

spots.name: Hanoi Weekend Night Market
spots.summary: A weekend market along Hang Dao toward Dong Xuan with cheap clothes and trinkets.
spots.tip: It runs Friday to Sunday evenings; keep bags zipped in the crowds.

spots.name: Bat Trang ceramic village
spots.summary: A pottery village with workshops and hundreds of ceramic shops.
spots.tip: Allow half a day; you can try throwing a pot.

spots.name: Hang Gai silk street
spots.summary: Silk shops and tailors selling scarves, ao dai and made-to-measure clothes.
spots.tip: Allow a few days for tailoring and at least one fitting.

spots.name: Nha Tho Street boutiques
spots.summary: Small design boutiques, lacquerware and ceramics near the cathedral.
spots.tip: Good for modern Vietnamese design rather than mass-produced souvenirs.

spots.name: Trang Tien Plaza
spots.summary: Hanoi’s upscale department store by the lake, with international brands.
spots.tip: Next to Trang Tien’s famous ice cream shop.

ho-chi-minh-city.note: Saigon shopping ranges from busy markets to design concept stores in renovated colonial apartment blocks.

spots.name: Ben Thanh Market
spots.summary: The city’s landmark market for coffee, lacquer, clothes and snacks.
spots.tip: Prices start high for tourists; compare a few stalls.

spots.name: Saigon Square
spots.summary: Indoor stalls of factory-overrun clothes, bags and sportswear.
spots.tip: Authenticity varies; check stitching and fit.

spots.name: 42 Nguyen Hue apartment block
spots.summary: An old apartment building filled with cafés and small fashion and design shops.
spots.tip: There is a small fee for the lift; stairs are free.

spots.name: Le Thanh Ton & Dong Khoi boutiques
spots.summary: Streets of tailors, lacquer, embroidery and Vietnamese designer boutiques.
spots.tip: Good for silk and linen with better finishing than the markets.

spots.name: Saigon Centre & Takashimaya
spots.summary: A modern mall with Japanese department store Takashimaya and international brands.
spots.tip: The basement food hall is great for packaged gifts.

siem-reap.note: Siem Reap shopping supports local crafts and social enterprises, plus lively night markets.

spots.name: Angkor Night Market
spots.summary: Evening stalls of scarves, carvings and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Bargain gently; many prices are in US dollars.

spots.name: Psar Chaa (Old Market)
spots.summary: The town’s old market for spices, kramas and everyday goods.
spots.tip: Morning is best for the food side.

spots.name: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market
spots.summary: A riverside night market of paintings, silk and carvings across the footbridge from Old Market.
spots.tip: Quieter than Angkor Night Market, which makes browsing easier.

spots.name: Kandal Village
spots.summary: A short street of boutiques, design stores and cafés.
spots.tip: Good for well-made textiles and homewares.

spots.name: Theam’s House
spots.summary: A gallery-workshop of a Cambodian artist selling lacquer art and design pieces.
spots.tip: Take a tuk-tuk; it combines well with a quiet afternoon.

ubud.note: Ubud is about handmade goods: silver, wood carving, textiles and boutique fashion along Jalan Monkey Forest and Hanoman.

spots.name: Ubud Art Market
spots.summary: Sarongs, baskets, carvings and souvenirs opposite the palace.
spots.tip: Go early in the morning for better prices and fewer crowds.

spots.name: Jalan Hanoman
spots.summary: A street of boutiques, yoga wear, homewares and cafés.
spots.tip: Linen and resort-wear boutiques are better value than at beach resorts.

spots.name: Celuk silver village
spots.summary: A village of silversmith workshops making Balinese jewellery.
spots.tip: Ask to see the workshop and check the silver stamp.

spots.name: Mas wood-carving village
spots.summary: Carving workshops and galleries along the main road.
spots.tip: Arrange shipping for large pieces with written terms.

spots.name: Threads of Life
spots.summary: A fair-trade gallery of natural-dye textiles woven across Indonesia.
spots.tip: Staff explain each textile’s origin; ask about their textile classes.

kuala-lumpur.note: Kuala Lumpur pairs giant malls in Bukit Bintang with craft halls and night markets.

spots.name: Petaling Street
spots.summary: A covered street market for cheap goods and snacks.
spots.tip: Many branded items are copies; buy for fun, not for labels.

spots.name: Central Market (Pasar Seni)
spots.summary: An art-deco hall of Malaysian crafts, batik and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Batik workshops nearby let you paint your own piece.

spots.name: Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur
spots.summary: A national craft centre with songket, batik, pewter and woodwork.
spots.tip: Prices are fixed, which saves haggling.

spots.name: Pavilion Kuala Lumpur
spots.summary: A big mall with everything from high street to luxury.
spots.tip: Linked by a covered walkway to KLCC.

spots.name: Suria KLCC & The Starhill
spots.summary: Luxury brands below the Petronas Towers and at Starhill.
spots.tip: Combine Suria KLCC with the park and towers.

beijing.note: Beijing shopping spans antique markets, hutong design shops and the luxury mall of Sanlitun.

spots.name: Panjiayuan Antique Market
spots.summary: A huge flea market of curios, books and crafts.
spots.tip: Weekend mornings are liveliest; many antiques are reproductions.

spots.name: Silk Street Market
spots.summary: Multi-floor stalls for silk, tailoring and bargains.
spots.tip: Hard bargaining is expected; check quality closely.

spots.name: Nanluoguxiang & Wudaoying hutongs
spots.summary: Hutong lanes with design shops, snacks and boutiques.
spots.tip: Wudaoying is quieter and more independent.

spots.name: 798 Art District
spots.summary: Former factories turned galleries with design shops.
spots.tip: Many galleries close Mondays.

spots.name: Taikoo Li Sanlitun
spots.summary: An open-air mall with flagships, streetwear and luxury labels.
spots.tip: The north section is the luxury side.

shanghai.note: Shanghai shopping is big and stylish, from fabric markets to boutiques in the former French Concession.

spots.name: South Bund Fabric Market
spots.summary: Tailors make suits, coats and qipao at good prices.
spots.tip: Allow several days and a fitting; bring a garment to copy.

spots.name: Tianzifang
spots.summary: Lanes of small shops, studios and cafés.
spots.tip: It gets crowded; arrive before noon.

spots.name: Anfu Road & Wukang Road
spots.summary: Tree-lined streets with concept stores, Chinese designers and cafés.
spots.tip: Weekend afternoons are busy but fun to people-watch.

spots.name: Nanjing Road East
spots.summary: A pedestrian shopping street of big stores leading to the Bund.
spots.tip: Walk it at night for the neon.

spots.name: IFC Mall & Plaza 66
spots.summary: Luxury malls with global flagships.
spots.tip: Plaza 66 on West Nanjing Road is the luxury core.

kathmandu.note: Kathmandu shopping is strongest in crafts: pashmina, thangka paintings, metalwork and trekking gear.

spots.name: Thamel trekking gear shops
spots.summary: Streets of trekking gear, some local-made, some copies.
spots.tip: Local brands like Sonam Gears offer better quality than generic copies.

spots.name: Asan Tole market
spots.summary: A busy old bazaar of spices, tea and everyday goods.
spots.tip: Watch your pockets in the crowds.

spots.name: Patan metalwork shops
spots.summary: Workshops near Durbar Square that cast Buddhist statues.
spots.tip: Ask about the casting method; hand-finished pieces cost more.

spots.name: Mahaguthi fair-trade shop
spots.summary: A fair-trade craft shop supporting Nepali artisans.
spots.tip: Fixed prices make it an easy first stop.

spots.name: Pashmina & thangka studios
spots.summary: Fine cashmere scarves and hand-painted thangkas.
spots.tip: Test pashmina labels; real pashmina is soft and not shiny.

istanbul.note: Istanbul pairs historic bazaars with modern malls and independent boutiques in Karaköy and Nişantaşı.

spots.name: Grand Bazaar side lanes
spots.summary: Beyond the main bazaar, lanes toward Mahmutpaşa sell bargains.
spots.tip: The main hall is pricier; walk outward for local prices.

spots.name: Spice Bazaar
spots.summary: Turkish delight, spices, tea and dried fruit.
spots.tip: Ask for vacuum-packing for travel.

spots.name: Kadıköy market & Moda
spots.summary: Food market streets plus vintage and record shops.
spots.tip: Take the ferry for the views.

spots.name: Karaköy & Galata boutiques
spots.summary: Concept stores and Turkish designer studios near the Galata Tower.
spots.tip: Pair with a coffee stop in Karaköy.

spots.name: Nişantaşı
spots.summary: Istanbul’s luxury district with global labels and Turkish designers.
spots.tip: Abdi İpekçi Street is the luxury spine.

rome.note: Rome is best for leather, artisan workshops and Via Condotti luxury, with vintage in Monti.

spots.name: Porta Portese flea market
spots.summary: Rome’s biggest Sunday flea market for clothes and curios.
spots.tip: Sunday mornings only; watch for pickpockets.

spots.name: Via del Corso
spots.summary: Long street of high-street brands and sneaker shops.
spots.tip: Weekends are packed; weekdays are easier.

spots.name: Monti boutiques
spots.summary: Vintage, independent designers and artisan workshops.
spots.tip: Mercato Monti runs on weekends.

spots.name: Via Margutta & Via dei Coronari
spots.summary: Galleries, antique dealers and artisan studios.
spots.tip: Many shops close for lunch.

spots.name: Via Condotti
spots.summary: Rome’s luxury street with Italian fashion houses.
spots.tip: Non-EU visitors can claim VAT refunds above the minimum.

florence.note: Florence is the place for leather, paper and artisan crafts, plus Italian luxury on Via de’ Tornabuoni.

spots.name: San Lorenzo leather market
spots.summary: Outdoor stalls of leather goods near the Central Market.
spots.tip: Check that leather is genuine; prices vary widely.

spots.name: Oltrarno artisan workshops
spots.summary: Workshops of bookbinders, jewellers and leatherworkers.
spots.tip: Santo Spirito and Via Maggio are good starting points.

spots.name: Scuola del Cuoio
spots.summary: A leather school selling handmade goods.
spots.tip: You can watch artisans at work.

spots.name: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella
spots.summary: A historic pharmacy selling perfumes and toiletries.
spots.tip: The rooms themselves are worth a look.

spots.name: Via de’ Tornabuoni
spots.summary: Florence’s luxury street, home to Gucci and Ferragamo.
spots.tip: The Ferragamo museum is also here.

venice.note: Venice shopping is about Murano glass, Burano lace, paper and masks, with luxury near San Marco.

spots.name: Rialto Market & stalls
spots.summary: Fish and vegetable markets plus souvenir stalls by the bridge.
spots.tip: Fish market closed Sundays and Mondays.

spots.name: Strada Nova
spots.summary: A broad street of everyday shops and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Cheaper than around San Marco.

spots.name: Mask workshops
spots.summary: Hand-made papier-mâché masks.
spots.tip: Look for workshops that let you see masks being made.

spots.name: Murano glass showrooms
spots.summary: Furnace showrooms selling glass.
spots.tip: Look for the Vetro Artistico Murano mark.

spots.name: Calle Larga XXII Marzo & the Mercerie
spots.summary: Italian fashion houses and fine jewellers on the lanes between San Marco and Rialto.
spots.tip: Non-EU visitors can claim VAT refunds above the minimum spend.

naples.note: Naples shopping is lively and local: street markets, nativity-figure workshops, tailoring and Via Chiaia boutiques.

spots.name: Mercato di Porta Nolana & Pignasecca
spots.summary: Noisy street markets of fish, produce, cheap clothes and kitchen goods, as Neapolitan as it gets.
spots.tip: Mornings are best; keep valuables close in the crowds.

spots.name: San Gregorio Armeno
spots.summary: The famous lane of nativity-scene workshops, with hand-made figures and lucky cornicello charms.
spots.tip: December is magical but packed; any other month is easier to browse.

spots.name: Via Toledo & Galleria Umberto I
spots.summary: Naples’ main shopping street of Italian high-street fashion, sneaker shops and the glass-roofed galleria.
spots.tip: Look inside Toledo metro station, one of Europe’s most striking.

spots.name: Limoncello, coral & ceramic shops
spots.summary: Small family shops along the old main street selling limoncello, coral cameos, ceramics and sweets.
spots.tip: Pack bottles in checked luggage, wrapped in clothing.

spots.name: Via Chiaia & Via dei Mille
spots.summary: Elegant boutiques, Neapolitan tailoring houses and Italian labels in the city’s smartest district.
spots.tip: Neapolitan ties and shirts are a classic splurge; ask about made-to-measure timing.

athens.note: Athens is good for leather sandals, olive-oil goods, jewellery inspired by antiquities and a buzzing flea market.

spots.name: Monastiraki Flea Market
spots.summary: Lanes of souvenirs, secondhand goods and antiques below the Acropolis, busiest on Sunday.
spots.tip: Avissinias Square is the antiques core; Sunday morning has the most stalls.

spots.name: Varvakios Central Market
spots.summary: The central market hall for olives, herbs, honey, nuts and spices at local prices.
spots.tip: Closed Sundays; mornings are liveliest.

spots.name: Ermou Street
spots.summary: A long pedestrian street of international high-street brands and sneaker stores from Syntagma Square.
spots.tip: Look for the tiny Byzantine Kapnikarea church in the middle of the street.

spots.name: Melissinos & Psyrri sandal makers
spots.summary: Workshops that cut and fit classic Greek leather sandals to your feet while you wait.
spots.tip: Allow a short wait for fitting and adjustments.

spots.name: Kolonaki boutiques
spots.summary: Upscale streets with Greek designers, fine jewellers such as Lalaounis and international labels.
spots.tip: Voukourestiou Street is the luxury spine; ask about VAT refunds.

santorini.note: Santorini shopping is small but special: Assyrtiko wine, ceramics, jewellery and art galleries in the cliff villages.

spots.name: Fira main lanes
spots.summary: The busiest lanes on the island for souvenirs, capers, fava and local snacks.
spots.tip: Shops stay open late in summer; mornings are less crowded.

spots.name: Pyrgos village shops
spots.summary: Quiet hilltop lanes with ceramics, handmade jewellery and small craft shops.
spots.tip: Much calmer than Oia and with similar views.

spots.name: Santo Wines shop
spots.summary: A cooperative winery shop with Assyrtiko, Vinsanto and local products.
spots.tip: Combine shopping with a caldera-view tasting at sunset.

spots.name: Oia galleries & Atlantis Books
spots.summary: Art galleries, designer jewellers and a much-loved independent bookshop in a cave house.
spots.tip: Shop before sunset; the lanes fill completely at dusk.

spots.name: Fira ‘Gold Street’
spots.summary: A lane of jewellers along the caldera walk, selling Greek gold and designer pieces.
spots.tip: Ask for a certificate, and compare a few shops before buying.

chania.note: Chania’s old town is great for leather, knives, olive oil and Cretan crafts.

spots.name: Chania Municipal Market (Agora)
spots.summary: A cross-shaped covered market hall for honey, herbs, cheese and olive oil.
spots.tip: Check it is open; it has been under long renovation in recent years.

spots.name: Skridlof Street
spots.summary: The old ‘leather street’, lined with bags, sandals and belts.
spots.tip: Quality varies a lot; check stitching and leather before buying.

spots.name: Sifaka Street knife makers
spots.summary: Traditional Cretan knife workshops, some engraving blades with mantinades verses.
spots.tip: Pack blades in checked luggage.

spots.name: Old Town design & ceramic shops
spots.summary: Small shops of ceramics, textiles and contemporary Cretan design in Venetian lanes.
spots.tip: Wander the lanes behind the western harbour.

spots.name: Venetian harbour jewellers
spots.summary: Jewellers selling Minoan- and Byzantine-inspired gold and silver.
spots.tip: Ask about the hallmark and where pieces are made.

paris.note: Paris covers everything: flea markets, concept stores in the Marais, department stores and the luxury of Avenue Montaigne.

spots.name: Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen
spots.summary: The world’s largest antiques and flea market, with a dozen markets from bric-a-brac to museum-grade furniture.
spots.tip: Open Saturday to Monday; Marché Vernaison is best for small finds.

spots.name: Le Marais
spots.summary: Concept stores, French labels, streetwear, vintage and tiny perfumers in old lanes.
spots.tip: Many shops here open on Sundays, unlike most of Paris.

spots.name: Rue de Rivoli & La Samaritaine
spots.summary: High-street brands along Rivoli plus the restored Art Nouveau Samaritaine department store.
spots.tip: Rue Saint-Honoré nearby has designer boutiques.

spots.name: Galeries Lafayette & Printemps
spots.summary: Grand department stores with luxury floors, food halls and free rooftop views.
spots.tip: Ask for tax-free paperwork at the store’s détaxe desk.

spots.name: Avenue Montaigne
spots.summary: Paris’s couture avenue of fashion houses from Chanel to Dior.
spots.tip: Window shopping is free; boutiques may ask you to queue on busy days.

london.note: London has some of the best streetwear and vintage in Europe alongside Bond Street and big department stores.

spots.name: Camden Market
spots.summary: Alternative fashion, vintage, crafts and street food by the canal.
spots.tip: Weekends are busiest; the Stables Market is the vintage core.

spots.name: Brick Lane & Spitalfields
spots.summary: Vintage warehouses, the Sunday Upmarket and Old Spitalfields Market’s makers.
spots.tip: Sunday is the best day for markets.

spots.name: Soho & Carnaby Street
spots.summary: London’s streetwear core: skate and sneaker shops, British labels and independent boutiques.
spots.tip: Drop days at streetwear stores bring queues; check the brand’s social media.

spots.name: Oxford Street, Selfridges & Liberty
spots.summary: Huge flagships, the Selfridges department store and Liberty’s Tudor-style building of prints and design.
spots.tip: Weekday mornings are calmer.

spots.name: Bond Street & Harrods
spots.summary: Luxury flagships on Bond Street and Harrods’ famous food halls.
spots.tip: The UK no longer offers tax-free shopping for visitors.

cairo.note: Cairo shopping is a bazaar experience, with cotton, papyrus, perfume oils and spices.

spots.name: Khan el-Khalili side alleys
spots.summary: The historic bazaar of lamps, spices, perfume oils, jewellery and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Bargain patiently, and walk away politely if a price is too high.

spots.name: Wekalet el-Balah
spots.summary: A local fabric market selling Egyptian cotton and linen by the metre.
spots.tip: Much cheaper than tourist shops for textiles.

spots.name: Tentmakers’ Street (Shareh el-Khayamiya)
spots.summary: A covered street where artisans hand-stitch colourful appliqué textiles.
spots.tip: Cushion covers pack flat and make good gifts.

spots.name: Zamalek boutiques
spots.summary: Egyptian designer stores and fair-trade craft boutiques on the island neighbourhood.
spots.tip: Good for crafts at fixed prices without haggling.

spots.name: Cairo Festival City & Mall of Egypt
spots.summary: Big modern malls with international and luxury brands.
spots.tip: Both are far from the centre; allow time for traffic.

luxor.note: Luxor shopping is smaller and more relaxed than Cairo: alabaster, spices and papyrus near the souk.

spots.name: Luxor Souk
spots.summary: A long souk near Luxor Temple with spices, scarves, galabiyas and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Bargain firmly but kindly; evening is cooler.

spots.name: Souk spice & tea stalls
spots.summary: Hibiscus (karkadeh), spices and herbal teas sold by weight.
spots.tip: Ask for sealed packets for travel.

spots.name: West Bank alabaster workshops
spots.summary: Workshops near the Valley of the Kings carving alabaster vases and statues by hand.
spots.tip: Real alabaster lets light through; machine-made stone does not.

spots.name: Papyrus galleries
spots.summary: Galleries selling painted papyrus artwork, often with demonstrations.
spots.tip: Real papyrus is flexible and does not crack when rolled.

spots.name: Winter Palace & Corniche hotel arcades
spots.summary: Jewellers and boutiques in the grand riverside hotels, with gold cartouches and fine cotton.
spots.tip: Ask for a certificate on gold and compare prices with the souk.

marrakech.note: Marrakech’s medina souks are a shopping adventure, with design concept stores in Gueliz for calmer browsing.

spots.name: Medina souks
spots.summary: Maze-like souks of leather, lanterns, spices, babouche slippers and textiles.
spots.tip: Bargain patiently; first offers can be several times the final price.

spots.name: Ensemble Artisanal
spots.summary: A government-run craft centre with artisans at work and fixed prices.
spots.tip: Visit first to learn fair prices before the souks.

spots.name: Souk Cherifia
spots.summary: A design hub inside the souks where young Moroccan brands sell at fixed prices.
spots.tip: A good break from haggling.

spots.name: Gueliz concept stores
spots.summary: Modern Moroccan design boutiques and concept stores in the new town.
spots.tip: 33 Rue Majorelle, near the Jardin Majorelle, gathers curated designers.

spots.name: Rug cooperatives & dealers
spots.summary: Berber rugs from mountain cooperatives and established dealers.
spots.tip: Shipping is common; get the price and delivery terms in writing.

fez.note: Fez shopping is craft-first: leather from the tanneries, ceramics, brass and weaving in the medina.

spots.name: Talaa Kebira
spots.summary: The main medina street of spices, slippers, sweets and crafts.
spots.tip: Download an offline map or hire a licensed guide; the medina is a maze.

spots.name: Chouara tannery leather shops
spots.summary: Leather shops with terraces overlooking the dye pits of the famous tannery.
spots.tip: Prices start high; leave politely if you feel pressured.

spots.name: Place Seffarine metal workshops
spots.summary: Coppersmiths hammering pots, pans and trays on a small square.
spots.tip: Good for practical kitchen pieces.

spots.name: Ain Nokbi ceramic cooperatives
spots.summary: Workshops of the famous blue-and-white Fez pottery and zellige tiles.
spots.tip: Ask for shipping quotes for big pieces.

spots.name: Weaving cooperatives
spots.summary: Hand-woven scarves, blankets and cactus-silk (sabra) textiles.
spots.tip: Ask to see the looms and how the fibre is made.

cape-town.note: Cape Town shopping is strong on local design, crafts and wine, from weekend markets to the V&A Waterfront.

spots.name: Greenmarket Square
spots.summary: A cobbled square market of African crafts, prints, beadwork and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Compare prices with the Watershed before buying.

spots.name: Neighbourgoods Market at the Old Biscuit Mill
spots.summary: A Saturday food and design market in a converted biscuit mill, with design shops around it all week.
spots.tip: Go Saturday morning; the market winds down by early afternoon.

spots.name: Bree & Long Street
spots.summary: South African labels, streetwear, vintage stores and cafés.
spots.tip: Bree Street is calmer and more design-led than Long Street.

spots.name: The Watershed
spots.summary: A big hall of South African designers, jewellers and craft makers.
spots.tip: Good for quality, fixed-price crafts in one stop.

spots.name: V&A Waterfront mall
spots.summary: International brands, jewellers and diamond shops by the harbour.
spots.tip: Visitors can reclaim VAT at the airport; keep receipts and goods handy.

nairobi.note: Nairobi is great for Kenyan crafts, beadwork and contemporary design.

spots.name: Maasai Market
spots.summary: A rotating open-air market of beadwork, kikoys, soapstone and carvings.
spots.tip: It moves between malls and days; check the current schedule before going.

spots.name: Toi Market
spots.summary: A huge secondhand clothing market (mitumba) with real bargains.
spots.tip: Go with a local; it is busy and chaotic.

spots.name: Kazuri Beads factory shop
spots.summary: Hand-made ceramic beads and pottery from a women’s workshop.
spots.tip: Free workshop tours show the whole process.

spots.name: Village Market
spots.summary: A relaxed mall with Kenyan designers and a regular Friday Maasai market.
spots.tip: The Friday market is the easiest craft market for visitors.

spots.name: Spinners Web
spots.summary: A craft collective showing quality Kenyan design, textiles and furniture.
spots.tip: A good single stop for gifts that are well made.

arusha.note: Arusha is a safari gateway, but it has good crafts, tanzanite and coffee for the trip home.

spots.name: Maasai Market & Curio Market
spots.summary: Stalls of carvings, beadwork, Tingatinga paintings and Maasai textiles.
spots.tip: Bargain firmly; start around half the opening price.

spots.name: Arusha Central Market
spots.summary: The local market for produce, spices and colourful kanga cloths.
spots.tip: Good for spices and kangas at local prices.

spots.name: Local coffee roasters & supermarkets
spots.summary: Tanzanian Arabica from the slopes of Kilimanjaro and Meru, sold by local roasters and in supermarkets.
spots.tip: Buy sealed whole beans; they travel better than ground coffee.

spots.name: Shanga
spots.summary: A social enterprise employing people with disabilities to make glass, jewellery and textile goods.
spots.tip: Combine with lunch before heading out on safari.

spots.name: Cultural Heritage Centre
spots.summary: A big gallery complex of African art, carvings and tanzanite jewellery.
spots.tip: Ask for a certificate with any tanzanite purchase.

cusco.note: Cusco is the best place in Peru for alpaca, textiles and Andean crafts, with San Blas artisans in the hills.

spots.name: San Pedro Market
spots.summary: A covered market of juice stalls, fruit, textiles and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Keep valuables zipped in the crowds.

spots.name: Centro Artesanal Cusco
spots.summary: A big hall of craft stalls with lower prices than the centre.
spots.tip: Compare quality between stalls; ‘alpaca’ is often a blend.

spots.name: San Blas artisan workshops
spots.summary: Hillside workshops of ceramics, carvings and religious art.
spots.tip: Ask whether work is made on site.

spots.name: Centro de Textiles Tradicionales del Cusco
spots.summary: A weaving cooperative with live demonstrations and fine textiles.
spots.tip: Prices are fixed and fair to the weavers.

spots.name: Kuna & Sol Alpaca
spots.summary: Premium baby alpaca and vicuña garments from Peruvian brands.
spots.tip: Check labels for baby alpaca and fibre percentages.

lima.note: Lima offers craft markets in Miraflores, designer shops in Barranco and premium alpaca.

spots.name: Mercado Indio
spots.summary: A large craft market along Avenida Petit Thouars with goods from all over Peru.
spots.tip: Compare a few stalls before buying alpaca.

spots.name: Gamarra
spots.summary: A huge garment district with very cheap clothing.
spots.tip: Go with a local; it is crowded and pickpockets work here.

spots.name: Barranco design shops
spots.summary: Peruvian design boutiques and galleries in a bohemian district, including Dédalo in an old mansion.
spots.tip: Pair with sunset at the Bridge of Sighs.

spots.name: Larcomar
spots.summary: A clifftop mall built into the Miraflores cliffs, with Pacific views.
spots.tip: Visit at sunset for the view.

spots.name: Kuna & Sol Alpaca
spots.summary: Premium baby alpaca and vicuña stores.
spots.tip: Ask about vicuña: it is the most exclusive fibre.

arequipa.note: Arequipa is the home of Peru’s alpaca industry, with fine yarns near Santa Catalina.

spots.name: San Camilo Market
spots.summary: The city’s main market, with fruit, cheeses and juice stalls.
spots.tip: Try a fresh juice at the counter.

spots.name: Fundo El Fierro craft market
spots.summary: A colonial courtyard full of craft stalls.
spots.tip: Compare quality before buying.

spots.name: Mundo Alpaca
spots.summary: A shop and free museum showing how alpaca is sorted, spun and woven.
spots.tip: Free to visit; live alpacas and llamas in the courtyard.

spots.name: Patio del Ekeko
spots.summary: A shopping complex of artisan shops, silver and alpaca.
spots.tip: Good for gifts in one place.

spots.name: Kuna & Sol Alpaca
spots.summary: Premium alpaca stores from Arequipa’s alpaca companies.
spots.tip: Check fibre labels for baby alpaca.

la-paz.note: La Paz has unique markets: witches’ market charms, Andean textiles and alpaca.

spots.name: Mercado de las Brujas
spots.summary: The witches’ market of charms, herbs and remedies.
spots.tip: Ask before photographing vendors.

spots.name: El Alto 16 de Julio market
spots.summary: One of South America’s biggest markets, running on Thursdays and Sundays.
spots.tip: Go with a local and leave valuables at the hotel.

spots.name: Calle Sagárnaga
spots.summary: A steep street of alpaca, weavings and crafts.
spots.tip: Quality varies; compare a few shops.

spots.name: Comart Tukuypaj
spots.summary: A fair-trade textile cooperative with fine weavings.
spots.tip: Fixed prices and fair pay for weavers.

spots.name: Sopocachi & Zona Sur designers
spots.summary: Bolivian designers and fine alpaca boutiques.
spots.tip: Zona Sur has the mall-style shopping.

rio-de-janeiro.note: Rio is great for beachwear, Havaianas and Brazilian design, from Ipanema boutiques to street fairs.

spots.name: Feira Hippie de Ipanema
spots.summary: A Sunday craft fair at Praça General Osório with art, leather and jewellery.
spots.tip: Sundays only.

spots.name: SAARA
spots.summary: A huge street market of cheap clothes, fabrics and carnival costumes.
spots.tip: Great for carnival costumes and accessories.

spots.name: Ipanema boutiques
spots.summary: Brazilian swimwear, beachwear and designer shops.
spots.tip: Rua Garcia D’Ávila is the high-end street.

spots.name: Feira de São Cristóvão
spots.summary: A northeastern Brazilian fair with music, crafts and food.
spots.tip: Weekends are best.

spots.name: Shopping Leblon & Village Mall
spots.summary: Rio’s upscale malls with Brazilian and international designer brands.
spots.tip: Village Mall has the biggest luxury names.

buenos-aires.note: Buenos Aires is known for leather, design boutiques in Palermo and San Telmo antiques.

spots.name: Feria de San Telmo
spots.summary: A Sunday street market of antiques and crafts along Calle Defensa.
spots.tip: Sundays only; tango dancers often perform in Plaza Dorrego.

spots.name: Feria de Mataderos
spots.summary: A gaucho fair of crafts, folk music and regional food on the city edge.
spots.tip: Check the schedule; it usually runs on Sundays.

spots.name: Palermo Soho
spots.summary: Argentine designer boutiques, streetwear and concept stores.
spots.tip: There is a weekend craft fair around Plaza Serrano.

spots.name: Calle Murillo leather outlets
spots.summary: A street of leather outlets for jackets, bags and shoes.
spots.tip: Ask about custom sizing and finishes.

spots.name: Avenida Alvear & Patio Bullrich
spots.summary: Luxury boutiques on Alvear and a polished mall in a former auction house.
spots.tip: Combine with Recoleta Cemetery.

santiago.note: Santiago shopping covers lapis lazuli, Chilean wine and design, with craft villages and big modern malls.

spots.name: Mercado Central & La Vega
spots.summary: The seafood hall and the huge La Vega produce market across the river.
spots.tip: Go before lunch, when La Vega is at its busiest.

spots.name: Los Dominicos craft village
spots.summary: A craft village of workshops for copper, lapis, leather and ceramics.
spots.tip: Best on weekends, when more workshops are open.

spots.name: Barrio Italia
spots.summary: Galerías of Chilean designers, furniture restorers and vintage stores.
spots.tip: Weekend afternoons are liveliest.

spots.name: Barrio Lastarria & Bellavista
spots.summary: Bookshops, design stores and lapis lazuli jewellers.
spots.tip: Ask whether stones are solid lapis or reconstituted.

spots.name: Costanera Center & Alonso de Córdova
spots.summary: A giant tower mall, plus the luxury boutique and gallery street of Vitacura.
spots.tip: Alonso de Córdova is the luxury street.

cartagena.note: Cartagena’s walled city is full of emerald dealers, hammocks and Colombian designer boutiques.

spots.name: Las Bóvedas
spots.summary: Former vaults in the city wall now full of craft shops.
spots.tip: Compare prices with Getsemaní stalls.

spots.name: Bazurto Market
spots.summary: A chaotic local market for fish, produce and street food.
spots.tip: Go with a guide.

spots.name: Getsemaní boutiques
spots.summary: Small shops, street art and craft stores in a lively neighbourhood.
spots.tip: Evenings are the liveliest time.

spots.name: Emerald jewellers
spots.summary: Colombia is famous for emeralds; the Walled City has many dealers and jewellers.
spots.tip: Ask for a certificate from an independent gem lab.

spots.name: Walled City designer boutiques
spots.summary: Colombian designers such as St. Dom and Silvia Tcherassi, with resort wear and accessories.
spots.tip: Prices are high, but the quality and design are excellent.

quito.note: Quito is the place for Panama hats, Otavalo-style textiles and Ecuadorian chocolate.

spots.name: Mercado Artesanal La Mariscal
spots.summary: A big craft market of textiles, hats and Andean crafts.
spots.tip: Bargain lightly.

spots.name: Mercado Central
spots.summary: The city’s historic food market, with juices, locro soup and fruit.
spots.tip: Try a fruit juice and locro de papa.

spots.name: Calle La Ronda
spots.summary: A restored colonial street of craft workshops and cafés.
spots.tip: Evenings are best.

spots.name: Ecuadorian chocolate shops
spots.summary: Single-origin Ecuadorian chocolate from brands such as Pacari and República del Cacao.
spots.tip: Bars travel well.

spots.name: Homero Ortega Panama hats
spots.summary: Genuine toquilla straw hats from Ecuador’s best-known maker.
spots.tip: Finer weaves cost much more; ask to see the grades.

puerto-iguazu.note: Puerto Iguazú is a small town, so shopping is mostly crafts, yerba mate and the duty-free shop.

spots.name: La Feirinha market
spots.summary: A market selling cheese, wine, olives and yerba mate.
spots.tip: Evenings bring local food and drinks.

spots.name: Guaraní craft stalls
spots.summary: Guaraní community crafts such as carved animals and woven baskets.
spots.tip: Buy direct to support communities.

spots.name: Avenida Victoria Aguirre shops
spots.summary: Main-street shops for mate gourds, leather and outdoor gear.
spots.tip: Good for mate sets.

spots.name: Hito Tres Fronteras craft fair
spots.summary: Craft stalls at the viewpoint where Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay meet.
spots.tip: Go for sunset views over the rivers.

spots.name: Duty Free Shop Puerto Iguazú
spots.summary: A large duty-free store with spirits, perfume and luxury goods.
spots.tip: Check customs limits for your country.

springdale.note: Springdale is a small gateway village to Zion, with galleries, outdoor gear and park bookshops.

spots.name: Zion Visitor Center bookstore
spots.summary: The park’s non-profit store for maps, field guides and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Proceeds support the park through the Zion Forever Project.

spots.name: Zion Park Boulevard gift shops
spots.summary: Small gift shops near the park entrance.
spots.tip: Good for postcards, stickers and park souvenirs.

spots.name: Zion Outfitter
spots.summary: Gear rental and outdoor clothing next to the park.
spots.tip: Rent Narrows gear here; book ahead in summer.

spots.name: Turquoise & silver jewellery shops
spots.summary: Shops selling Southwest silver and turquoise jewellery.
spots.tip: Ask whether pieces are artist-made and look for a maker’s mark.

spots.name: Springdale art galleries
spots.summary: Galleries selling landscape paintings and photography of the canyon.
spots.tip: Ask about shipping framed work.

flagstaff.note: Flagstaff mixes outdoor shops, Route 66 souvenirs and Native American arts.

spots.name: Downtown Route 66 shops
spots.summary: Route 66 souvenirs, vintage stores and gift shops in a historic downtown.
spots.tip: Walk San Francisco Street and Route 66.

spots.name: Flagstaff Community Market
spots.summary: A seasonal farmers market with local food and crafts.
spots.tip: Sunday mornings in season.

spots.name: Babbitt’s Backcountry Outfitters
spots.summary: An outdoor gear shop in a historic downtown building.
spots.tip: Good for last-minute Grand Canyon gear.

spots.name: Downtown Native art galleries
spots.summary: Galleries with Hopi, Navajo and Zuni jewellery, pottery and rugs.
spots.tip: Ask for artist information and provenance.

spots.name: Museum of Northern Arizona shop
spots.summary: A museum shop selling authentic Hopi, Navajo and Zuni art.
spots.tip: Pieces come with artist information.

moab.note: Moab is outdoor-gear country, with rock shops, an indie bookshop and local art.

spots.name: Moab rock shops
spots.summary: Shops of fossils, minerals and dinosaur souvenirs.
spots.tip: Kids love them.

spots.name: Back of Beyond Books
spots.summary: An independent bookstore with a strong Southwest and Edward Abbey section.
spots.tip: Good for trail guides and maps.

spots.name: Moab Farmers Market
spots.summary: A seasonal farmers market with local produce and crafts.
spots.tip: Check the season dates.

spots.name: Main Street gear shops
spots.summary: Gear shops for hiking, mountain biking and canyoneering.
spots.tip: Rent mountain bikes and get trail advice here.

spots.name: Moab galleries
spots.summary: Galleries of landscape photography and local art.
spots.tip: Ask about shipping larger works.

jackson.note: Jackson Hole has western wear, galleries and outdoor gear, with fine art around the Town Square.

spots.name: Jackson Hole People’s Market
spots.summary: A summer farmers market with local food and crafts.
spots.tip: Wednesdays in summer.

spots.name: Western wear shops
spots.summary: Shops of boots, belts, hats and western clothing.
spots.tip: Try boots on; sizing differs by brand.

spots.name: Teton Mountaineering
spots.summary: Climbing and outdoor gear with knowledgeable local staff.
spots.tip: Ask for trail and conditions advice.

spots.name: Town Square galleries
spots.summary: Galleries of western and wildlife art.
spots.tip: Summer gallery walks are a fun evening.

spots.name: Jackson Hole Hat Company
spots.summary: A workshop making handmade custom cowboy hats.
spots.tip: Custom hats take time; order ahead.

mariposa.note: Mariposa is a small Gold Rush town with local crafts and gear for Yosemite.

spots.name: Historic Main Street shops
spots.summary: Antique and gift shops in Gold Rush-era buildings.
spots.tip: Combine with the history centre.

spots.name: Mariposa Museum & History Center shop
spots.summary: A small shop of Gold Rush history books and gifts.
spots.tip: The museum has a small entry fee.

spots.name: California State Mining & Mineral Museum shop
spots.summary: A museum shop selling minerals and gold specimens.
spots.tip: Check opening days.

spots.name: Yosemite Valley Village store
spots.summary: Groceries, gear and souvenirs inside the park.
spots.tip: Prices are higher than outside the park; stock up in Mariposa.

spots.name: Main Street galleries
spots.summary: Art galleries with Yosemite landscapes and local crafts.
spots.tip: Ask about shipping framed work.

las-vegas.note: Las Vegas shopping is mostly casino malls and outlets, with vintage and local makers in the Arts District.

spots.name: Las Vegas North Premium Outlets
spots.summary: A big open-air outlet mall with designer and sportswear discounts.
spots.tip: Check the outlet’s visitor centre for extra coupons.

spots.name: Arts District vintage shops
spots.summary: Vintage clothing, records and maker shops along Main Street.
spots.tip: First Friday brings an evening street festival.

spots.name: Grand Canal Shoppes
spots.summary: A canal-themed mall with gondolas and painted skies.
spots.tip: Fun to walk even if you are not buying.

spots.name: Forum Shops at Caesars
spots.summary: Luxury and designer brands in a Roman-themed mall.
spots.tip: Look out for the free animatronic fountain shows.

spots.name: The Shops at Crystals
spots.summary: Top luxury flagships on the Strip.
spots.tip: The free tram links it to nearby resorts.

medellin.note: Medellín is Colombia’s fashion capital, with strong local brands, textile districts and design boutiques.

spots.name: El Hueco
spots.summary: A dense shopping district of cheap clothes, shoes and everything else.
spots.tip: Go in the morning and keep valuables hidden.

spots.name: Plaza Minorista
spots.summary: A big traditional market for tropical fruit, flowers and produce.
spots.tip: Try exotic fruits like lulo and granadilla.

spots.name: Mercado de San Alejo
spots.summary: A monthly craft and antiques fair in the city centre.
spots.tip: Usually on the first Saturday of the month.

spots.name: Provenza boutiques
spots.summary: Colombian designer labels, streetwear and concept stores.
spots.tip: Evenings are lively with cafés and bars.

spots.name: El Tesoro & Santafé malls
spots.summary: Upmarket malls with Colombian and international brands.
spots.tip: El Tesoro has views over the valley.

mexico-city.note: Mexico City is a shopping city: huge markets, crafts from every state and design stores in Roma and Condesa.

spots.name: Mercado de La Ciudadela
spots.summary: A big market of crafts from every state, from textiles to Talavera pottery.
spots.tip: Good for textiles, alebrijes and pottery.

spots.name: La Lagunilla
spots.summary: A sprawling Sunday flea market of antiques, vintage and curios.
spots.tip: Sundays only; go early.

spots.name: Fonart
spots.summary: The government craft store with high-quality pieces at fair, fixed prices.
spots.tip: Check its prices before shopping in markets.

spots.name: Roma & Condesa boutiques
spots.summary: Mexican designers, concept stores, streetwear and vintage shops.
spots.tip: Colima and Córdoba streets are good starting points.

spots.name: Avenida Presidente Masaryk
spots.summary: Polanco’s luxury avenue of global flagships.
spots.tip: Pair with Museo Soumaya and Museo Jumex nearby.

hiroshima.note: Hiroshima shopping centres on covered arcades and local crafts like Kumano brushes and Miyajima rice paddles.

spots.name: Hondori shopping arcade
spots.summary: A long covered arcade of fashion, drugstores and cafés near Peace Park.
spots.tip: Easy shopping when it rains.

spots.name: Miyajima Omotesando shopping street
spots.summary: Rice paddles, momiji manju sweets and grilled oysters on the island.
spots.tip: Ferries take about 10 minutes from Miyajimaguchi.

spots.name: Hiroshima Station ekie
spots.summary: A station mall with local gifts and food.
spots.tip: Good for last-minute souvenirs before the train.

spots.name: Kumano brush shops
spots.summary: Shops selling Kumano makeup and calligraphy brushes.
spots.tip: Hakuhodo is a famous brand.

spots.name: Sogo & Fukuya department stores
spots.summary: Department stores with designer brands and local gifts.
spots.tip: Their basements sell beautifully packaged local sweets.

nara.note: Nara shopping is gentle and crafty: calligraphy ink, sake, deer souvenirs and the old Naramachi quarter.

spots.name: Higashimuki shopping arcade
spots.summary: A covered street of souvenirs, deer goods and snacks.
spots.tip: Next to Kintetsu Nara station.

spots.name: Mochiidono shopping street
spots.summary: A local shopping street with snacks and small shops.
spots.tip: Near Nakatanidou, famous for fast-pounded mochi.

spots.name: Naramachi
spots.summary: Old merchant townhouses with craft shops and cafés.
spots.tip: Weekdays are quiet and easy to explore.

spots.name: Harushika sake brewery
spots.summary: A sake brewery with a shop and tastings.
spots.tip: A small fee covers a tasting of several sakes.

spots.name: Kobaien ink makers
spots.summary: A historic sumi ink maker founded in 1577.
spots.tip: Book an ink-making workshop in advance.

busan.note: Busan pairs giant traditional markets with Shinsegae Centum City, one of the world’s biggest department stores.

spots.name: Gukje Market & Bupyeong Kkangtong Market
spots.summary: Huge traditional markets with clothes, goods and street food.
spots.tip: Kkangtong’s night market is best for snacks.

spots.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
spots.summary: Korea’s biggest fish market.
spots.tip: Buy seafood downstairs and eat it upstairs.

spots.name: Seomyeon underground shopping
spots.summary: Underground arcades of cheap K-fashion and accessories.
spots.tip: Handy in the rain.

spots.name: Jeonpo Café Street
spots.summary: Indie shops, stationery and cafés in an old tool-market area.
spots.tip: Weekend afternoons are liveliest.

spots.name: Shinsegae Centum City
spots.summary: A giant department store with luxury brands and a spa.
spots.tip: Spa Land is popular; ask about tax refunds.

da-nang.note: Da Nang is mostly a beach city, but it is the gateway to Hoi An’s tailors and has big local markets.

spots.name: Han Market
spots.summary: A central market for dried goods, coffee and clothes.
spots.tip: Upstairs has fabrics and clothing.

spots.name: Con Market
spots.summary: A big local market with street food and household goods.
spots.tip: More local than Han Market and with lower prices.

spots.name: Vincom Plaza Da Nang
spots.summary: A modern mall by the river.
spots.tip: Good in the rain.

spots.name: Hoi An tailors
spots.summary: Hoi An is famous for quick, made-to-measure tailoring.
spots.tip: Allow at least two days and one fitting.

spots.name: Marble Mountains carving shops
spots.summary: Workshops of stone carvings, from small figures to garden statues.
spots.tip: Shipping is often available; get terms in writing.

dubai.note: Dubai shopping ranges from old souks to the world’s biggest malls.

spots.name: Spice Souk & Textile Souk
spots.summary: Old souks for spices, dates, frankincense and fabric.
spots.tip: The abra ferry across the creek costs very little.

spots.name: Karama Market
spots.summary: Bargain clothes, bags and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Many branded items are copies.

spots.name: Deira Gold Souk
spots.summary: Gold jewellery priced by weight and workmanship.
spots.tip: Prices follow the daily gold rate; negotiate the making charge.

spots.name: Alserkal Avenue
spots.summary: Galleries and concept stores in converted warehouses.
spots.tip: Many places close on Mondays.

spots.name: Dubai Mall
spots.summary: One of the world’s biggest malls, with luxury fashion and an aquarium.
spots.tip: Fountain shows run every evening.

barcelona.note: Barcelona shopping blends independent boutiques in El Born and Gràcia with Passeig de Gràcia’s luxury.

spots.name: Mercat dels Encants
spots.summary: One of Europe’s oldest flea markets, under a mirrored roof.
spots.tip: Open Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays.

spots.name: El Raval vintage shops
spots.summary: Vintage and skate stores along Carrer de la Riera Baixa.
spots.tip: Watch your pockets.

spots.name: El Born boutiques
spots.summary: Independent designers and concept stores in medieval lanes.
spots.tip: Shops open late morning.

spots.name: Gràcia shops
spots.summary: Local boutiques and design shops in a village-like neighbourhood.
spots.tip: Great for an afternoon wander with cafés.

spots.name: Passeig de Gràcia
spots.summary: Luxury flagships along a boulevard of Gaudí buildings.
spots.tip: Non-EU visitors can claim VAT refunds.

milan.note: Milan is Italy’s fashion capital, from markets and streetwear to the Quadrilatero della Moda.

spots.name: Mercato di Viale Papiniano
spots.summary: A street market with clothes, shoes and sometimes designer seconds.
spots.tip: Tuesday and Saturday mornings.

spots.name: East Market
spots.summary: A monthly vintage and secondhand market in a former factory.
spots.tip: Check the date online; it runs on selected Sundays.

spots.name: Corso Buenos Aires
spots.summary: One of Europe’s longest shopping streets, packed with high-street and sneaker shops.
spots.tip: Weekday mornings are calmer.

spots.name: 10 Corso Como
spots.summary: A famous concept store with fashion, design and books.
spots.tip: It has a courtyard café and gallery.

spots.name: Quadrilatero della Moda
spots.summary: Milan’s luxury fashion district of Italian fashion houses.
spots.tip: Non-EU visitors can claim VAT refunds.

zanzibar.note: Zanzibar shopping is about Stone Town’s spices, carved doors, kangas and Tingatinga art.

spots.name: Darajani Market
spots.summary: The main market for spices, fruit and fish.
spots.tip: Mornings are best.

spots.name: Gizenga Street shops
spots.summary: Shops of kangas, carvings and souvenirs.
spots.tip: Bargain lightly and politely.

spots.name: Spice farm shops
spots.summary: Shops at spice farms selling vanilla, cloves and cinnamon.
spots.tip: Buy sealed packets for travel.

spots.name: Tingatinga art shops
spots.summary: Shops of colourful Tanzanian Tingatinga paintings.
spots.tip: Paintings roll up for travel.

spots.name: Doreen Mashika
spots.summary: A Zanzibar designer boutique of fashion and accessories.
spots.tip: Pricier, but unique pieces.
